moves.headline: HP jumps 11.5% as results and a cautious outlook prove better than investors had feared
moves.summary: HP rose 11.5% to $31.15 the day after reporting fourth-quarter revenue up 9.3% to $16.0 billion, guiding fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $3.15–3.45 and raising its quarterly dividend to $0.31. Adjusted quarterly EPS fell 10.8% as memory costs hit PC margins.
why: The numbers were not strong on their own: PC units fell 29%, the Personal Systems margin was 3.0% and adjusted fourth-quarter EPS dropped to $0.83. But revenue grew 9% as HP passed higher memory prices on to customers, full-year adjusted EPS of $3.33 beat its own range, and free cash flow reached $3.3 billion.

Expectations were very low going in. The shares traded at roughly 8 to 9 times adjusted earnings, below the average analyst target, after months of worry that memory and storage costs would wipe out PC profits. A fiscal 2027 range that is roughly flat at the midpoint, plus $2.9–3.1 billion of expected free cash flow and a higher dividend, was enough for a relief rally.
